reviewer: gpt-6-luna; independent static source/control-flow and bound-executable inspection

reviews.summary: The parsed iteration count is passed to spmvGpu, and the constructed CSR has n=floor(dim²/sparsity) stored entries with the terminal row offset n. The chosen short-row variant has width 2/4/8/16/32 selected from average nnz per row; the long-row variant is selected at average>=256. Short rows use 128-thread groups with a capped grid and a row grid-stride loop, and each group accumulates the whole CSR interval in width strides before one lane stores the row. Long rows use 128 threads, a row grid-stride loop and per-thread nonzero stride of blockDim.x, followed by reduction and store. The host builds a graph of 64 launches when iterations>1, warms up once outside timing, then times iterations/64 graph launches and iterations%64 direct launches; with no graph it times exactly iterations direct launches. Compiled spmvGpu retains these branch/count paths and calls cudaLaunchKernel with the selected kernel pointer, block/grid and argument array; the timed event end and synchronization follow the final launches. All five width-specific and the long-row native sm86 kernels inspected through their arithmetic backedges, reductions/stores and function exits. No omission identified.

source_evidence.claim: CUDA build target and optimization flags.

CSR initialization/count; short and long kernel coverage; actual selected kernel/grid/argument dispatch; graph batch, warmup, timed quotient/remainder and output handling; CLI iteration parsing and full input setup.

compiled_evidence.claim: Complete optimized spmvGpu host function: selected kernel pointer and cudaLaunchKernel calls, capture and warmup/synchronization, timed graph quotient loop and direct remainder, event stop/synchronization and result transfer.
All five selected native sm86 short-row kernels and the long-row kernel through arithmetic/backedges, reductions, row stores and exits.

reviews.notes: Capped short-row grid is paired with the kernel row grid-stride loop; no rows are dropped by the cap. No runtime tests or benchmark evidence used.
